transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Saturday, August 8. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Government opens dialogue with aspirants as protest enters Day 14, says talks 'positive'. Group Seeks Concrete Decisions On All Major Demands By Aug 10 India rejects US criticism of FCRA Bill; MEA calls it 'internal matter'. The government is set to expedite the Foreign Contributions Regulation Act, which focuses on managing foreign funding for organizations. In contrast to criticism from a US Congressman regarding proposed changes, the administration remains resolute. Home Minister Amit Shah has met with church leaders to resolve their issues. The Bill's discussion and possible approval in Parliament are imminent. Thailand school shooting: Teen kills grandparents at home, 5 at campus. In a tragic event, a teenage student opened fire at a Thai school on Friday, claiming five lives. Prior to the school shooting, he also killed his grandparents. Authorities reported 23 individuals were injured during this violent episode. The weapon used was his grandfather's firearm, unleashing a barrage of shots. 'I got angry': Ashwin reveals why he stopped talking to Sanjay Manjrekar. Ravichandran Ashwin opened up about the initial sting from Sanjay Manjrekar's critical comments, which fueled his desire to elevate his fitness and refine his bowling. Manjrekar later praised Ashwin in an article, acknowledging his remarkable performances. As a testament to his skill, Ashwin concluded his career as India's second-highest international wicket-taker with 765 wickets, solidifying his status as one of the country's finest all-rounders, still active in T20 leagues. How WhatsApp clue, Mygate trail help CBI crack NEET paper leak. A WhatsApp conversation triggered the CBI's probe into the NEET-UG examination scam. Subject matter experts colluded by memorizing exam questions and distributing them to students for a fee. Tracking through Mygate app logs and WhatsApp groups led investigators to the involved students and question setters. Additionally, papers were smuggled to Rajasthan, where coaching centers disseminated the leaked materials. Elon Musk's preferred state halts data center approvals; says 'prove' this. Texas Governor Greg Abbott has ordered a temporary halt to new data center approvals. Regulators must complete a comprehensive audit before projects can move forward. Developers must prove electricity and water use, and tax incentives. Abbott stated Texans must come first in all state decisions. 27 Arunachal border locations get standard names to snub China's renaming attempts. India has taken a decisive step by officially naming twenty-seven sites in Arunachal Pradesh on its maps, a move designed to clarify territorial boundaries and counter Chinese assertions. These sites represent key historical moments related to border conflicts, featuring important mountains and villages along the McMahon Line, helping to raise awareness of India's rightful claims on these significant lands. India counters China's 'map war', assigns official names to 27 Arunachal sites. India ahs onsistently rejected Beijing's practice of assigning Chinese names to places in Arunachal Pradesh, describing the exercise as "vain and preposterous". India has maintained that such actions do not change the "undeniable" fact that the state "was, is, and will" remain an integral part of the country. Several of the newly marked locations hold strategic importance because of their proximity to the Line of Actual Control (LAC). US sanctions Dubai-based crypto exchange over alleged IRGC funding. The United States sanctioned Dubai-based Shelbit for processing millions for Iran's state entities. This action targets sanctions evasion through cryptocurrency networks, as announced by the Treasury Department. Shelbit allegedly facilitated transactions for Iran's central bank and the IRGC. The exchange denied all allegations and stated operations ceased in January 2026. Michael Dell's son Zach Dell wants his Base Power batteries in every American backyard. Zach Dell's company Base Power is expanding its home battery business across America. The company offers a unique membership model, replacing high upfront costs. Base Power recently secured one billion dollars in new funding, valuing it at thirteen billion. This expansion includes plans for international markets like the United Kingdom and Germany. I and B ministry eyeing framework to regulate OTT content. The I and B ministry is exploring new legislation targeting OTT platforms. This proposed framework prioritizes the regulation of offensive content while preserving users' rights. Plans include implementing robust age verification mechanisms and parental controls. Additionally, an independent review panel will be tasked with evaluating flagged content following its release and determining appropriate sanctions for any breaches of the established guidelines.
